intended_object: A predicate on a type `F` of bundled functions `R → S` between semirings with monoid actions. It says every `f : F` is a ring homomorphism and is `φ`-semilinear, i.e. `f (m • r) = φ m • f r`. In other words, `F` is a class of `φ`-equivariant ring homomorphisms. This comes from the docstring and from the class's relation to `MulSemiringActionHom`.
explanation:
The class combines two existing classes. `DistribMulActionSemiHomClass F φ R S` gives the equivariance law `map_smulₛₗ` (`f (c • x) = φ c • f x`) and additivity. `RingHomClass F R S` gives preservation of `0`, `1`, `+` and `*`. Together these are exactly the axioms of a `φ`-equivariant ring homomorphism.

The class assumes only `DistribMulAction` on the semirings, not `MulSemiringAction`. That is weaker, so the class is if anything more general; it is not narrower. This is Mathlib's own class from the standard morphism-class hierarchy (the `…SemiHomClass` pattern), and Mathlib has no separate, more general version of it.

One small flaw: the docstring calls it `MulSemiringActionHomClass`, which is the name of the abbreviation for the case `φ = id`. This is a naming slip and does not change what the class means.
